leading_positions.synthesis: Four members put optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) in their round-1 configuration. Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson make it their whole prize with a near-identical citation on the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks; Pearce includes it as one half of a two-part configuration (see the B001 plus B021 entry). Shared: the magic-wavelength idea, independent confirmation at the 1e-18 level across many laboratories, and the cleanest two-name credit on the shortlist. Not shared: how distinct the lattice clock is from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes (all four supporters concede this is the main risk), whether the pending redefinition of the second argues for waiting or for recognising now, and whether Lemonde, Ludlow, Lemke, Takamoto and Derevianko are unfairly left out. Kroll and Lindroth disclose field proximity (see flags). Danielsson says he could place it first if a sharper statement of what the lattice clock showed beyond earlier prizes can be made; Eriksson and Johansson defer on that question.

Three members put topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect in their round-1 configuration, and Danielsson and Johansson say they moved it up after reading colleagues' openings. All agree on the confirmation record (HgTe edge channels in 2007, ARPES, STM, many independent groups over 15 to 20 years), the generality of the bulk-invariant idea, and that the topic is mature and arguably overdue. They do not agree on laureates: Danielsson and Mehlig name Kane, Mele and Molenkamp; Johansson names Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, and stresses that Hasan's 3D work would otherwise go unrecognised. All three describe the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as an unresolved cost, and Danielsson and Johansson say that if no defensible trio exists the case weakens. Eriksson, Olsson, Kroll and Pearce each name B024 as an alternative but are not counted as supporters of this configuration.

Eriksson alone puts magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene in his configuration (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Andrei), as a theory-plus-experiment story reproduced by many groups with a clear new platform. Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson list it as an alternative but do not prefer it. Challenged by Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce on maturity (eight years, unsettled pairing mechanism, twist-angle disorder). Eriksson himself flags that dropping Bistritzer from the three names is a real cost and the choice among Bistritzer, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei is open.

The chair's own configuration is a two-part prize, optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) plus IceCube high-energy neutrinos (Halzen alone), as two distinct achievements from different subfields. No other member includes B021 in a configuration; Danielsson ranked IceCube first in his opening but moved to B024 and keeps B021 as an alternative. Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Danielsson all question the single-name Halzen credit against a collaboration of hundreds with AMANDA and DUMAND precursors, and Eriksson also questions source-identification maturity. The chair acknowledges this is the weakest link and says he would prefer B024 as a main prize if condensed-matter colleagues find a fair allocation.

areas_of_agreement: Independent confirmation is treated as essential and is regarded as strong for B001 (many laboratories comparing clocks at about 1e-18), B024 (transport, ARPES and STM over 15 to 20 years) and the IceCube diffuse flux; it is acknowledged for B013 for the phenomena but not for their interpretation.

Attribution, not scientific merit, is the main obstacle that members themselves name for B024 (Mele versus Hasan, and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang outside the list), B021 (a single name for a collaboration with predecessors), B013 (Bistritzer versus Andrei) and, less severely, B001 (Lemonde, Ludlow, Lemke and others).

Members who support B001 and members who support B024 each describe the other as the strongest competing case and say they would not obstruct it on scientific grounds, so the dispute is over relative weight and allocation, not over soundness.

The 2016 topological-phases prize is regarded by Johansson, Mehlig, Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce as context rather than a barrier to B024, though Eriksson and others want the citation to make the distinction explicit.

Several members (Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth) want any B001 citation anchored on the magic-wavelength lattice clock itself rather than on records or on the comb, and Olsson would keep practical-impact language out of it.

No member proposes a prize for B007, B027, B029 or B041 in their round-1 configuration; B029 appears only as Johansson's alternative (with his stated reservations and disclosed connection), B027 only as Kroll's alternative, and B041 only as an alternative for Lindroth and Mehlig.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a distinct discovery (magic-wavelength condition, many-atom regime with ion-level systematics) or an extension of the comb (2005) and ion-clock (2012) precision-measurement lineage. Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson argue it is distinct; Danielsson and Eriksson ask for a sharper statement of what was shown that was not already known.

Whether a measurement or instrument achievement should weigh as much as a new class of matter or organising concept (Kroll and Pearce, instrument-driven; Mehlig, concept-driven; Danielsson, nature supplying the clue).

Whether the 2D quantum spin Hall result and the 3D topological insulator observation are one discovery under a single bulk-invariant prediction (Mehlig, Johansson) or separable steps, with the 3D step a follow-on (Danielsson, Olsson).

Whether the unresolved source classes behind the IceCube diffuse flux (TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane rest on few objects) matter for recognising the discovery of the flux itself (Eriksson raises this, Pearce proposes citing the diffuse flux).

Whether the superconducting pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder in magic-angle graphene mean the discovery is understood well enough (Eriksson says the phenomena are robust; Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson doubt it).
attribution_disputes: B024: Mele is argued by Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson to be inseparable from Kane as co-author of the founding papers and the Z2 invariant, while Johansson prefers Hasan to represent the 3D observation; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal, Zhang deceased) and Fu, Moore and Balents are outside every proposed trio.

B021: Halzen alone against the IceCube collaboration, AMANDA and DUMAND precursors, and later spokespersons and directors who are not credited; Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson raise this and Pearce calls it his weakest link.

B013: three of Bistritzer, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei; Eriksson drops Bistritzer, whom he calls the first author of the prediction, and Olsson and Pearce question the basis for including Andrei.

B001: Katori credited for the proposal and first strontium realisation, Ye for the accuracy frontier; Lemonde, Ludlow, Lemke, Takamoto, Derevianko and Bloom are uncredited, and Olsson notes that the record accuracy is shared among several laboratories and will be superseded.

Similar proposals differ in laureates: the three B024 configurations use two different trios (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp versus Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan), and the three B001-only configurations differ only in citation wording; Pearce's two-part configuration alone credits a single person for B021.
maturity_disputes: B013 is about eight years from the 2018 experiments with an unsettled pairing mechanism; Eriksson thinks the phenomena are mature, whereas Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce would rather wait.

B001: the redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce read as either a reason to wait or a dependence rather than a precondition; no member has argued that the discovery is immature.
B024 is described by Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig as mature and arguably overdue, but Eriksson and Pearce say that cannot be settled without a defensible allocation of names.
B021: the diffuse flux is described as firm, while source-class identification is incomplete.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson discloses that he is director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, a theorist in the Chalmers superconducting-circuits community, and ranked B029 (circuit QED) first in his opening; he has placed it only as an alternative and invites the committee to discount his views on B029.

Kroll discloses that he spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, that Jun Ye is at JILA where Hall worked, and that his precision laser spectroscopy background makes him close to the field of B001; he reports no joint work or supervision with Ye or Katori.

Lindroth discloses her close collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and the Lund and ETH Zurich attosecond groups (none credited on the shortlist) and says her atomic-structure background may make her sympathetic to B001, B041 and B029.

Pearce (chair) discloses field familiarity with IceCube through the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and the astroparticle community, with no stated collaboration or personal link to Katori, Ye or Halzen, and has a configuration that includes B001 and B021.

Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson note a shared Chalmers or Gothenburg environment that is institutional only; Danielsson and Eriksson report no specific conflict, and Mehlig and Olsson report none for any credited name.
questions_for_round2: B001: Can the supporters state in a sentence what the lattice clock demonstrated that the comb (2005) and ion-clock (2012) prizes did not, so that Danielsson, Eriksson and Johansson can decide whether it is a distinct discovery, and should the citation name the magic-wavelength lattice explicitly?

B024: Do the condensed-matter members converge on a single trio, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp or Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, and if not, what is the reason, given that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are outside every option?
B024: Does a prize for the quantum spin Hall effect alone leave the 3D topological insulator observation unrecognised at an acceptable cost, as Johansson asks, and should the citation say so?

B021: Is there a defensible way to credit IceCube with at most three names, or should the committee drop IceCube from the configuration; would Pearce and Danielsson name additional laureates or limit the citation to the diffuse flux?

Configuration: Should the committee decide between a single-topic prize (B001 or B024) and a two-part prize, and if the latter, which combination is acceptable when B024 would then have a single name and B001 plus B021 would credit three people?

B013: Is there evidence of robustness of the correlated phases across laboratories despite twist-angle disorder that would change the maturity assessment for Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, and how should Bistritzer and Andrei be treated?
Timing: Does the pending redefinition of the second weigh for, against, or not at all in recognising B001 now?
Conflicts: How should the committee treat the disclosed field proximity of Kroll and Lindroth on B001, Johansson on B029, and the chair's familiarity with IceCube when it counts positions in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: The eight configurations form three groups: B001 alone (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson), B024 (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, with two different trios), and singletons for B013 (Eriksson) and for the chair's B001 plus B021 pairing. Danielsson and Johansson say they moved to B024 after reading the opening ballots. The explicit round-1 configurations show no majority for any single ballot item: B001 has four supporters counting the chair's pairing, B024 has three. Members outside each group generally name the other as a fallback (B024 is an explicit alternative for Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce), so the question is how allocation and distinctness are resolved, not whether either is scientifically sound. The outstanding questions are mostly about names and distinctness from earlier prizes.
